page5_img_1.png.title: Mapping best practices to reviewer challenges
page5_img_1.png.description: A two-column table that maps reported code-review challenges to the specific best-practice items (coded A=Author, R=Reviewer, O=Organization) that may help. The lower, fully visible section titled “To address reviewer challenges:” lists rows such as “Large reviews are hard to manage” → A1.2; “Finding time to do reviews” → A1.1, A1.4, A1.5, A1.6, A2.1, R3.1, R3.2; “Understanding a change and its motivation” → A1.2, A1.3, A1.4; “Finding relevant documentation” → A1.4, A1.5; “Understanding history of changes, decisions” → O4, R4.2, A5.5; “Insufficient training for reviews” → O6, R3.5; “Reviewing not valued enough” → O1, O3; and “Unsure of impact on job evaluations” → O3. The top of the image shows a partially visible author-focused mapping (e.g., “Receiving insightful feedback” → R3.4, R3.5; “Find reviewers” → A2.2–A2.5), and the table uses alternating light-blue rows with a darker blue header to organize the challenge-to-practice mappings.

page4_img_1.png.title: Infographic: Code Reviewing Best Practices for Authors, Reviewers, and Organizations
page4_img_1.png.description: A one-page infographic (Figure 2) divided down the center into an Author column (left) and Reviewer column (right) with icons and arrows showing an iterative review flow. The Author side lists labeled practices A1, A2, A5 and A6 (e.g., A1: “Prepare code change for review” with items like “Be conscientious,” “Aim for small, incremental changes,” and “Test/analyze before submitting”; A2: “Select and notify reviewers” with guidance on how many and who to notify; A5: “Respond and iterate” including “Show gratitude” and “Track and confirm suggested changes”; A6: “Commit code change” urging documentation and reflection). The Reviewer side lists R3 and R4 (R3: “Accept and conduct code review” — e.g., “Set dedicated, bounded time,” “Review frequently, fewer changes at a time,” “Focus on core issues first”; R4: “Provide feedback” — e.g., choose communication channels carefully, give constructive reasons for rejections, use tools that provide decision traceability). A bottom Organization section enumerates seven recommendations (build positive review culture, develop/revise policies, count review time, provide appropriate tools, promote checklists, provide training, and monitor bottlenecks), reinforcing that these practices are intended to address the author- and reviewer-facing challenges identified in the paper.

page2_img_1.png.title: Survey results: demographics, participation, motivations, and ranked challenges in Microsoft code reviews
page2_img_1.png.description: A vertically arranged infographic summarizing survey responses from 911 of 4,300 invited Microsoft developers, showing respondent experience and code-review activity. Key demographics: 87% have 2+ years in the software industry, 70% have 6+ years, 40% have 10+ years; 72% have worked at Microsoft 2+ years; 80.3% report 2–5 years of code-review experience (10+ years also reported by 22%). Participation over the previous week: 39% acted as a reviewer at least once per day (36% a couple times that week), whereas only 17% authored reviews daily (48% a couple times); motivations ranked highest are code improvement (1), finding defects (2), and knowledge transfer (3). Ranked challenges place receiving feedback in a timely manner as the top problem (1), followed by review size (2) and managing time constraints (3), with 13 specific challenge items listed in descending priority.
